🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
pkg/operator/starter.go (1)
`240-246`: _🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🔵 Trivial_ | _⚡ Quick win_ **Make the matcher exact-match safe.** `regexp.MustCompile("^" + cond + "$")` only stays exact while `cond` has no regexp metacharacters. Quoting the input keeps this helper correct if the condition set changes later.
♻️ Suggested fix ```diff func inertiaForCondition(cond string, duration time.Duration) status.InertiaCondition { return status.InertiaCondition{ - ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile("^" + cond + "$"), + ConditionTypeMatcher: regexp.MustCompile("^" + regexp.QuoteMeta(cond) + "$"), Duration: duration, } } ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate. In `@pkg/operator/starter.go` around lines 240 - 246, The matcher in inertiaForCondition is not truly exact-safe because cond is interpolated directly into a regexp, so any metacharacters would change its meaning. Update inertiaForCondition to build the ConditionTypeMatcher with a quoted version of cond instead of raw string concatenation, while keeping the same exact-match intent. This change should be made in the helper that returns status.InertiaCondition and uses regexp.MustCompile. ```
